clue.text: Bring back a popular music form and do some drumming

indicators.note: to bring back is to send something the way it came, so the two words are read from the end

parts.note: rap is a popular music genre
to do someone is to cheat them, as is to diddle

explanation.surface: A musician revives an old pop style and plays the drums along with it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bring back' turns A and RAP into PARA.
explanation.definitionFit: A drumming rudiment of alternating single and double strokes, so it is some of a drummer's work.

clue.text: Eg bull shows endless anger goring her, say, badly

indicators.note: goring means piercing, so one piece is driven into the other
badly means the letters are put in disorder
the last letter is removed

parts.note: ire is anger

explanation.surface: A bull shows rage by goring a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts IRE to IR, which gores (goes into) AYRSHE, the anagram of HER SAY signalled by 'badly'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ayrshire is a Scottish breed of dairy cattle, so a bull may be one.

clue.text: One that flies from a part of NW Europe

parts.note: the UK lies in north-west Europe

explanation.surface: Something departs from a corner of north-west Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: A seabird of northern waters; most species fly, unlike the extinct great one.

clue.text: Public banquet duke dismissed in private

indicators.note: the duke is sent away from the meal, so his letter goes

parts.note: a formal dinner is a public banquet

explanation.surface: At a public banquet a duke was dismissed in private.
explanation.definitionFit: Inner thoughts are private ones, kept within and not shown.

clue.text: Like a fellow throwing money round pub when upset

indicators.note: the money goes round the pub

parts.note: dosh is slang for money

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: an inn is a pub

explanation.surface: A man throws cash around a bar after getting upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Like a fellow' is the definition: a fellow is a college academic. 'upset' reverses the pub in this down clue; 'throwing' is just surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A fellow is a university don, and donnish means scholarly in the manner of an academic.

clue.text: Purse found by former inspector, say

parts.note: ex means former

indicators.note: say shows the word is chosen for how it is spoken, not spelt

parts.note: a checker is one who inspects

explanation.surface: A wallet is found by an ex-inspector.
explanation.definitionFit: The national treasury or public funds, so figuratively the public purse.

clue.text: Hack is an ill-mannered person

definitions.meaning: to hack something is to stand or tolerate it
a surly, grumpy individual is likened to a large growling animal

explanation.surface: A journalist is called rude.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: 'can't hack it' means can't tolerate it, and a gruff boor is called a grizzly beast.

clue.text: Stunning creature's clothing rather extravagant

indicators.note: the creature clothes, or wraps round, the other word

parts.note: a being is a creature
wilder means more extravagant

explanation.surface: An animal wears quite flamboyant clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Stunning in the sense of dazing or confounding someone, leaving them perplexed.

clue.text: Short answer to short sort of clue?

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for answer
being short with someone is being cross or curt

explanation.surface: A brief answer to a terse crossword clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossword clues come in two kinds by direction, and this is one of them.

clue.text: Trained bird half-heartedly in country

indicators.note: the bird is placed inside the name of the country

parts.note: Benin is a country in West Africa

indicators.note: half of the bird's heart, its doubled middle letter, is lost

parts.note: a rook is a black bird of the crow family

explanation.surface: A trained bird lives somewhere abroad, but is not fully committed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-heartedly' removes only one of the bird's two central letters, half its heart; the result goes in just after the country's first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse or new shoe that is broken in has been trained or worn into proper shape.

clue.text: Chicken or fish not cooked inside sent back

indicators.note: the reversed word goes within the fish

parts.note: cod is a common food fish

indicators.note: sent back means the word is written the other way round

parts.note: raw food has not been cooked

explanation.surface: A diner sends back a chicken or fish dish because it is undercooked inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chicken' looks like part of the menu with the fish, but it is the definition; 'sent back' reverses the uncooked word before it goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicken is the playground word for someone lacking courage, a scaredy-cat.

clue.text: Person uncovering worthless group

definitions.meaning: one who shows or reveals something
British slang for a contemptible, useless bunch of people

explanation.surface: A flasher is part of a disreputable gang.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is read as show-er, someone who shows.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang 'what a shower!' dismisses a hopeless lot; literally the word is also one who displays.

clue.text: Turn on cold radiator - -can then take this off?

definitions.text: Turn on cold radiator - -can then take this off?

parts.note: to wind is to turn, as with a key
C is short for cold on taps
a heater is a radiator

explanation.surface: If you put the heating on, you can take your jacket off.
explanation.definitionFit: A windproof jacket that you would shed once the heating warms the room.

clue.text: Dreamer at sea sailed in it

indicators.note: at sea means confused or all over the place, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A romantic sailed away on a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' rearranges the letters of SAILED and IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone guided by lofty, impractical ideals is a dreamer or visionary.

clue.text: Where theatregoers are seated in rows — not just H

definitions.text: Where theatregoers are seated in rows — not just H

parts.words: Where theatregoers are seated in rows — not just H
parts.note: the theatre's audience area, and a joke that the literal opening of the word house is just its first letter H

explanation.surface: Audience members sit in rows of a theatre, and not only row H.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not just H' teases the literal reading: the front of 'house' is H, but the theatre phrase means the whole audience area.
explanation.definitionFit: The theatrical term covers the auditorium and foyers where the public is, as opposed to backstage.

clue.text: Bubbly drink with an edge or a cocktail

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixture, so the words are mixed together

explanation.surface: A fizzy drink makes an edgy cocktail.
explanation.definitionFit: A fizzy orange-flavoured soft drink.

clue.text: Jam I have regularly with new organist

parts.note: a jam is a mess, a tight spot

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter is taken

explanation.surface: Someone has jam, as often as possible, with something new.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes I, A and E from 'I have'.
explanation.definitionFit: Olivier Messiaen was a French composer and long-serving church organist in Paris.

clue.text: Go with head man on newspaper out to lunch

parts.note: to have a go is to have a crack
the brain is in the head, and 'head' is used for intellect
ED is short for editor, the boss of a newspaper

explanation.surface: An editor heads out to lunch with the paper's top man.
explanation.definitionFit: Out to lunch is slang for crazy or not all there, as is a hare-brained, mad person.

clue.text: Number to look up? There's a catch in it

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from the bottom

parts.note: ten is a number
to peek is to look

explanation.surface: You look up a phone number, but there's a snag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns TENPEEK round as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: An angler's net keeps fish alive in the water, so the day's catch is held in it.

clue.text: China supports ruling for prisoner

indicators.note: in a down clue, the piece that supports sits below the other

parts.note: the party in power is in
china is rhyming slang for mate (china plate)

explanation.surface: China backs a judgment about a prisoner.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney rhyming slang: 'china plate' rhymes with mate, a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: An inmate is a resident of a jail, a prisoner.

clue.text: Con could make living with ease on the outside

indicators.note: the letters could be made into something new, so they are rearranged
only the outside letters of the word are used

explanation.surface: A fraudster could make a living easily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the outside' gives E and E from 'ease'; 'could make' rearranges them with LIVING.
explanation.definitionFit: To con someone is to trick or wheedle them into something, the same as cajoling by deceit.

clue.text: Ship heading off slowly extremely slowly

indicators.note: the heading, or first letter, is cut off

parts.note: largo is the musical direction for a very slow tempo
the first letter of the musical term

indicators.note: only the extreme letters, first and last, of the second slowly are used

explanation.surface: A ship sets off very, very slowly.
explanation.walkthrough: LARGO without its head gives ARGO; the ends of 'slowly' give SY.
explanation.definitionFit: An argosy is a large merchant ship, originally from Ragusa (Dubrovnik).

clue.text: Vehicle say clearly stopped halfway

indicators.note: stopping halfway through the word means its second half is cut off

parts.note: to articulate is to say clearly

explanation.surface: A lorry driver tells you clearly that it pulled up halfway.
explanation.walkthrough: ARTIC is British for an articulated lorry, a truck with a separate tractor cab.
explanation.definitionFit: An articulated lorry is a heavy goods vehicle.

clue.text: University seen behind graduate with books and a gown

indicators.note: the university letter comes after the graduate and books

parts.note: MA is a Master of Arts, a graduate
NT is the New Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: At a university a graduate gets books and a gown.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose seventeenth-century woman's gown or mantle, named after the Italian city.

clue.text: Citizen has love for one American capital? That's hypothetical

indicators.note: the love letter takes the place of the capital letter

parts.note: a national is a citizen of a country
the capital letter of American, its A
love is zero in tennis, written O

explanation.surface: A citizen loves an American capital city, which sounds a bit theoretical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one American capital' is the initial A of 'American', not a city; O replaces one A of NATIONAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something existing only in theory or imagination is merely notional, a synonym of hypothetical.

clue.text: High honour overwhelms Henry, the physicist

indicators.note: overwhelms suggests surrounding and engulfing the other letter

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit, a high British honour
H is the symbol for henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: A top award goes to a scientist named Henry.
explanation.definitionFit: Georg Ohm was a German physicist after whom the unit of resistance is named.

clue.text: Equipment producing illegal drugs

definitions.meaning: kit or tackle for an activity

explanation.surface: Kit used in making illegal drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means kit or apparatus, and in slang it also names narcotics.

clue.text: Attraction of two couples in mid twenties bonding

indicators.note: two pairs of letters from the middle of the word are taken

parts.note: cement bonds things together

explanation.surface: Two couples in their mid twenties are attracted and bond.
explanation.walkthrough: The four central letters of 'twenties' give ENTI.
explanation.definitionFit: An enticement is a lure or temptation, something that attracts.
